behavioral_effects: Dependabot PR runs skip the three Codecov upload steps, so test, test-frontend, Governance tool, and CI OK no longer fail on 'Not valid tokenless upload'; the six open Dependabot PRs can go green on their real signal.
compatibility_impact: None for code. Coverage telemetry: Dependabot-triggered runs stop uploading backend/frontend/governance flags to the self-hosted Codecov; pushes to main and human PR runs are unchanged, so trend data on main is unaffected.
follow_up: When the next human PR runs, check its upload step; if it also fails tokenless, add override_branch github.head_ref to the three steps or fix the instance config, and consider removing this actor guard.
limitations: Root cause on the Codecov instance side is undiagnosed: it rejects PR-event uploads from Dependabot runs even with a valid token freshly copied from the instance config (fork-format branch label forcing the tokenless path is the suspect). Whether human same-repo PR uploads succeed is still unverified - no such PR has run with a token present.
Verified by workflow linters only; the behavioural proof is the next Dependabot rebase going green.
reason: All six open Dependabot PRs fail test, test-frontend, and Governance tool at the Codecov upload step: the instance rejects PR-event uploads with 'Not valid tokenless upload' even with a valid 36-char token from the Dependabot secrets store, and fail_ci_if_error turns that into a red CI OK; coverage floors already gate locally in pytest/vitest so the upload is telemetry, not a gate
rollback: git revert the commit; the guard is three step-level if conditions plus a comment.
security_impact: None. The change narrows when a coverage upload runs; no new secret exposure, and the CODECOV_TOKEN secret remains referenced only by the same pinned codecov-action steps.
summary: Skip self-hosted Codecov uploads on Dependabot runs so dependency PRs stop failing CI on coverage telemetry
